layer0.description: Bastrop-county-side cohort, currently wired via layerWhere
layer0.reading: The filter matches 100% of the layer's own features. There is no null, differently-cased, or differently-spelled CITY_LIMIT value being dropped. Mechanism (b) -- the layerWhere filter silently excluding polygons that exist -- is RULED OUT for layer 0. Whatever is missing for Bastrop's 26 is not a filter defect on this layer.

layer1.description: Travis-county-side sliver (service metadata name: "City of Elgin Zoning: Travis County"), the named follow-on, not wired
layer1.reading: Layer 1 exists and is almost entirely CITY_LIMIT='ELGIN' (499/500); one feature carries a blank/whitespace value, not null and not a case variant. If layer 1 were wired with the same layerWhere pattern it would pick up at most 499-500 parcels total across its whole extent.

decisiveFinding: Travis's 1,680 unaccounted parcels cannot be resolved by wiring layer 1 alone: layer 1 holds only 500 features total, so even a perfect point-in-polygon match against every one of them accounts for at most ~500 of the 1,680. At least ~1,180 Travis parcels have no candidate polygon in either layer regardless of any code fix. Combined with layer 0's filter matching 100% of its own features (mechanism b ruled out there), this points toward mechanism (3b) -- a real coverage gap in Elgin's published GIS -- for a substantial share of both counts, consistent with the hauska-factory declaration's arealPct of 56.82%. This is not yet confirmed for the specific 26 Bastrop parcels; that requires the point-in-polygon test against layer 0 (dispatch step 2), which is next.
nextStep: Point-in-polygon the 26 named Bastrop parcels against live layer 0 (and, for completeness, layer 1) to get a parcel-level answer rather than an aggregate one; independently derive and spot-check the Travis 1,680 set the same way.
